messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pierce <j.pierce@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: FinEx - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification / next steps

Hi Jordan / Sanjay

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps on the performance / SLO side so we can size Dedicated capacity accurately: 

Key requirements you confirmed:
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 250ms (streaming enabled for live feed)
- Typical request shape: 4-8 prompts per user interaction, average 120 tokens input, expected 250 token outputs
- Concurrency: ~50 steady concurrent users during business hours; concurrency can spike to 250 during market-open bursts
- QPS / tokens: steady-state ~6 QPS (75 QPS total across all users) equating to ~18k tokens/sec aggregated (assume average 300 tokens per second per concurrent stream when streaming)
- Peak bursts: short 3-5 minute bursts up to 900 concurrent users (rush), estimate peak QPS ~900
- Streaming: yes - low-latency partial-token streaming is required for the trader dashboard

I attached a quick workbook with two sizing models (steady vs peak) and the assumptions I used (20270721-finex-throughput-estimates.xlsx). Please review and highlight any mismatches in the token sizes or burst assumptions.

Next steps:
1) Jordan / Sanjay: confirm payload sizes (avg input/output tokens) and whether all requests require streaming.
2) Redwood: run an internal micro-benchmark mapping your numbers to our GPU configs and share expected tokens/sec and estimated GPUs for steady and peak.
3) If numbers align, we’ll propose a Dedicated pool with an autoscale buffer and suggested fallbacks (cheaper quantized variant + optional regional fallback).

Thanks - I looped Marissa on infra sizing and will bring Neha in if we move to SLO/contract terms.
— Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael - good recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 250 token output is our average; we see heavy tails up to 800 tokens for detailed summaries but that’s ~5% of requests. Will that change sizing materially?
- Streaming: ideally streaming for all interactive flows; batch report generation can be non-streaming.
- Concurrency: 50 steady users is accurate for desk usage; the spikes to 900 are real during earnings windows (2-3 times per quarter). Spikes last ~1-6 minutes.

I attached a short note with our token distribution (will send separate). For now please size with 250 avg / 800 tail.

Jordan

j.pierce@finex.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pierce <j.pierce@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FinEx - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification / next steps

Appreciate the details, Jordan - helps a lot. Quick notes based on the 250/800 distribution:

- Tail impact: with 5% of requests at 800 tokens the steady-state GPU needs increase ~12-18% vs using average only. For peak bursts the tail matters more for memory/KV cache pressure.
- Streaming cost: streaming can slightly increase observed CPU-side latency but lowers perceived latency for end-users; we’ll include streaming-friendly kernels in the sizing.
- Suggested starting config (rough):
  - Steady: 2 x A100-80GB-class instances (or equivalent) with continuous-batching + prefix cache to meet p95<250ms at 50 concurrent users and the given token mix
  - Peak buffer: autoscale to ~10 instances for burst cover (short-lived autoscale to handle 900 concurrent users; will recommend warm pool and fast spin-up)

I uploaded the sizing workbook with the assumptions and a per-GPU token/sec estimate. See the attachment referenced in the previous email. If it looks reasonable I’ll schedule an infra benchmark (we run your sample workload against equivalent infra to validate).

FYI looping Neha for SLO/ops input and Marissa for capacity planning.

- Rafael

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: FinEx - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification / next steps

Rafael / Marissa -

Quick internal note after reviewing Jordan's numbers:
- I recommend we model two SLO tiers in the proposal:
  1) Standard: p95 < 250ms, 99.5% availability, no cost for small periodic bursts (<5 minutes, up to 2x steady concurrent)
  2) Premium burst protection: same latency SLOs but includes a paid warm-pool + guaranteed autoscale cap for earnings windows (handles 900 concurrent for up to 10 minutes)
- For the proposal we'll provide expected GPU count (steady & peak), plus an ops checklist: warm pool sizing, pre-warm signals, fallback model variants, and observability hooks (token-level tracing).

I'll help draft the SLO language and attach the recommended warm-pool policy before next call.

-Neha
